towerTypes.name: Stepped setback tower
towerTypes.claim: Cream tower with vertical fluting that steps back in tiers to a narrow top; the most common tall type, both as block towers and filling the background skyline.

towerTypes.name: Tapered rocket or bullet tower
towerTypes.claim: Smooth, rounded tower tapering to a point like a rocket or shell, with little setback; shown in pairs or as a single glazed teal tower.

towerTypes.name: Saucer spire
towerTypes.claim: Slim shaft carrying one or more disc-shaped saucer decks near the top, finished by a needle; several stand together on one block, and the same form appears as a hotel tower at street level.

towerTypes.name: Skyport tower
towerTypes.claim: One tower with several stacked circular landing decks cantilevered around the shaft, small craft parked on and flying near them, and rocket-like spires at the top.

towerTypes.name: Machine-crowned tower
towerTypes.claim: Setback towers whose tops carry dishes, red-and-white lattice masts and antennae rather than an architectural finish; a whole block of them is shown.

towerTypes.name: Round-cornered banded slab or drum
towerTypes.claim: Mid-height streamline building with curved corners and horizontal bands of window and balcony, sometimes cylindrical and glazed; lower than the spired towers around it.

towerTypes.name: Arched-fin tower
towerTypes.claim: Tower with a round-arched top outlined in coral vertical stripes, standing at a block edge or as a neighbour rather than the central tower.

towerTypes.name: Megastructure blocks (not towers, but they carry towers)
towerTypes.claim: A stepped ziggurat of planted terraces with towers rising behind it, and a raised slab on giant legs carrying a park, a lake and two towers above a lower city beneath.

crowns.name: Needle or spire
crowns.claim: Thin pointed spire, often gold, finishing stepped setback towers and tapered towers; the default crown across the background skyline.

crowns.name: Starburst
crowns.claim: Gold radiating star on a mast, carried by a stepped setback tower in the aerial view and by a clock tower and a free-standing pylon at street level.

crowns.name: Atom or orbit rings
crowns.claim: Sphere with orbit rings on a mast, carried by a lower tower in the aerial view and by low and stepped civic buildings at street level; a larger ring version wraps a dome.

crowns.name: Saucer or ring disc
crowns.claim: Horizontal disc or halo ring near the top of a slim shaft, usually with a needle above it; carried by saucer spires and by the stepped tower over the rail.

crowns.name: Machine crown
crowns.claim: Dishes, red-and-white lattice masts and antennae on the top of setback towers; a red lattice mast also appears as a secondary element on other blocks.

crowns.name: Landing decks with rockets
crowns.claim: Stacked circular decks with a cluster of rocket-like spires above, shown only on the skyport tower.

crowns.name: Lantern or small dome
crowns.claim: Small domed or lantern cap, sometimes teal or gold, on secondary towers and podium corners rather than on the tallest tower.

crowns.name: Stepped fin crown
crowns.claim: Stack of coral and cream vertical fins stepping up to a point, carried by the tower the rail passes through; a neon-outlined version tops the cinema front.

railMeetsBuilding.name: Through the tower
railMeetsBuilding.claim: The elevated rail passes straight through the base of the block's central tower above the podium roof, entering on one side and leaving on the other, with a train on the line.

railMeetsBuilding.name: Glazed hall on the podium
railMeetsBuilding.claim: Beside the pierced tower, a glazed barrel-vaulted hall sits over the rail on the podium roof, reading as the station enclosure.

railMeetsBuilding.name: Viaduct on pylons past the frontage
railMeetsBuilding.claim: A single-beam rail on slim pylons curves around the tower's low podium above street level, with shopfronts and pedestrians continuing underneath.

railMeetsBuilding.name: Terminal hall with clock tower
railMeetsBuilding.claim: A stand-alone terminal of repeated pointed shell vaults with a clock tower; trains run on at least two raised levels beside it and a rounded platform canopy projects over one track, with a pedestrian terrace and stairs below.

railMeetsBuilding.name: Elevated ways at the block edge
railMeetsBuilding.claim: Elevated ways on piers run past the block without entering it; whether they are rail or road is not readable at this size.

railMeetsBuilding.name: Enclosed bridge between buildings
railMeetsBuilding.claim: A glazed tube bridge links two buildings above the street, and a high arch links two towers; neither shows a train, so they read as walkways rather than rail.

composition.name: Towers rise from a shared podium
composition.claim: Each block is a continuous low podium with rounded corners and street frontage all round; towers stand on or inside it rather than meeting the street directly, and the podium roof carries pools, gardens and domes.

composition.name: Tallest toward the centre or back, low at the street
composition.claim: Height steps up from the street edge to the block's interior or rear; the perimeter stays low and the tallest element sits inboard.

composition.name: One dominant with lower companions
composition.claim: A block has a single clearly tallest tower with smaller towers or drums beside it.

composition.name: Clusters of two to five with unequal heights
composition.claim: Where towers of one type group, they come as a pair, a trio or a cluster of four or five, with heights and crowns varied within the group rather than matched.

composition.name: One theme per block, with one mixed exception
composition.claim: Seven of the eight blocks hold to a single tower or crown theme; one block deliberately mixes saucer, setback, glazed drum and lattice mast.

composition.name: Dense backdrop of setback towers
composition.claim: Behind every block the skyline is a dense, hazy field of stepped setback towers with needle crowns, against which the themed block stands out.

composition.name: Street-level buildings are a low centre tower with symmetric wings
composition.claim: At street level, single buildings are shown as a central stepped tower or pylon flanked by low rounded wings, with a forecourt of water or paving in front.

notDecidable: Heights and storey counts: no scale, dimensions or level markers on either sheet, so tower height bands and height ratios within a block can only be read as relative.
Which tiles are Harbour: no tile is labelled with a district, and only blocks/mixed_skyline and atomic/grand_hotel show open water at the edge.
Whether the eight block themes are alternatives for one site or types meant to sit side by side, and how often each should occur across a district.
Spacing between tower blocks and how themed blocks are placed relative to each other, the water or the road hierarchy: each aerial tile shows one block in isolation.
Rail level and whether it matches the sky concourse: the rail is shown elevated, but its height against the podium and deck levels is not given.
Whether the tower the rail passes through contains a stop, or the rail only passes through; no platform is visible in blocks/rail_through.
Rail network layout: no tile shows a line beyond one block, so routes, stop spacing, interchanges and whether the terminal in atomic/monorail_terminal is an end of line are not shown.
Whether the elevated ways in blocks/machine_crowns are rail or road, and whether the tube bridge in blocks/mixed_skyline and the arch in blocks/hanging_terraces are walkways.
No street-level tram is clearly shown on either sheet, so how a tram stop meets a building cannot be drawn from them.
Whether crown type signifies building use: the sheets show crowns on hotels, a terminal, a café and civic buildings without a consistent rule.
The two sheets differ in view and rendering (aerial blocks against street-level single buildings), and no tile ties a street-level building to a place in an aerial block.
atomic/hotel_lobby and atomic/fashion_arcade are interiors and give no skyline information.
